A saber frame lasts 0.025

. A swing's strength depends on how far the hilt moves in one saber frame. A saber lock moves forward at most once in each saber frame.

A blade starts at the hilt in the character's hand and moves with the character's animations. A character with one lightsaber holds it in the
hand. A second lightsaber goes in the

hand. A double-bladed lightsaber has a blade at each end. Swords, vibroblades and staves have blades of a fixed length.

Each end of a quarterstaff, double-bladed sword or vibro double-blade is 0.71 meters long.

A swinging blade damages every character it passes through. A single attack deals at most one damage
of the weapon to each target. The blade must pass through 4.1 meters of the target's body to deal the full damage
. Any cut deals at least 50% of the damage

. The target takes the damage when the blade leaves the body or when the attack ends.

A blade is checked for hits every 0.2 meters along its length.

Two blades clash when they pass within 0.41 meters of each other's tip and path.

When a blade turns through a wide angle in a single moment, the game checks for hits along the arc. Each check is 0.33 of the turn further along.

A blade must pass through 4.1 meters of a body in one attack to deal its full damage

.

A blade's first cut on a target deals at least 50% of the damage
. Further cuts in the same attack add the rest, up to the full

.

Some moves swing the blade through a target several times. These are the katas, the butterflies, the spins and the jump attacks of two weapons and of the double-bladed lightsaber. In these moves, each time the blade goes through a target counts as one pass. A blade that goes back into the target within 0.15

of leaving it is still in the same pass.

In a move of several swings, each pass of the blade through a target deals up to 150% of the damage of an ordinary attack. This way, every swing that hits the target deals damage.

A move of several swings deals at most 150% of one ordinary attack's damage to each target, even when every swing hits. The extra damage makes up for the longer time the move keeps the attacker busy.

An attacking blade hits any character or object within 0.051 meters of its edge.
is a number that decides who wins when two blades meet. An attacking blade's power is its style's
multiplied by 2, plus 1. The blade gains 1 more power for each step of distance its hilt moves in one saber frame.

power is never below 1 and never above 16. Each move also has a move power of its own. The move power depends on the move and on how far into the move the character is.

The fast style is
1, the medium style
2 and the strong style

3. Two weapons and a double-bladed lightsaber count as medium.

A special attack is a named move such as a kata, a jump attack, a flip, a spin or a back attack. A special attack deals damage and clashes with other blades only in the middle of its move, not at its start or its end. Outside that time its blade does no harm.

A character who is not attacking blocks attacks, blaster bolts and thrown lightsabers that come from within the character's block arc. The block arc is the area in front of the character where blocks are possible. The arc is wider at a higher defense
. It is also wider against blades than against bolts. A character with no defense

does not block.

A character blocks an attack when the cosine of the angle between the attack and the character's facing is above a limit. The limit is 0.9 at defense
2 and 0.3 at

3. A lower limit means a wider arc.

Against a blade or a thrown lightsaber, the block arc's limit is 0.25 lower, so the arc is wider.

When two blades meet, or a character blocks an attack, the game goes through the outcomes below in order. The first outcome that applies happens. First, the defender may knock the attack away. Second, the attacker may break the defender's parry. Third, the attacker may bounce off a strong parry. Fourth, if both characters are attacking, the one with more power breaks the other's attack or makes it bounce. If none of these happens, the defender parries. A strong enough attacker then crushes the parry, and a weaker one is turned aside.

In co-op, a player on another machine sees the world a little late. The game checks that player's shots and blades against other characters where the player saw them, up to 0.4
in the past. When a blade hits a player who could block it, the game waits up to 0.1

for that player's block.

A blade's
on a player on another machine waits up to 0.1

for that player's block.

A character who attacks with a lightsaber or a melee weapon moves slower than normal. How much slower depends on the saber style and on the attack. The character is slowest while backing off, faster in a spinning attack, and fastest while attacking forward. In the strong style, the character also moves slower between attacks.
